record.narrative:
All newly delivered context-robustness and specificity tests have valid Welch cells and can be judged against the +0.10 signed lower-bound benchmark. The PIK3CA-pathway context checks are decisive: TP53-loss cells continue to show a clinically meaningful weaker-dependency shift for dependency_USP7 in both PIK3CA-wildtype (H187, signed lower bound +0.314) and PIK3CA-mutant cells (H188, signed lower bound +0.238). KEAP1-loss continues to show clinically meaningful weaker dependency for dependency_NFE2L2 in both PIK3CA strata (H189 lower +0.770; H190 lower +0.769), and SMARCA4-loss continues to show clinically meaningful stronger dependency for dependency_SMARCA2 in both strata (H191 lower +0.763; H192 lower +0.735). These results support persistence of the central associations across common co-occurring PI3K-pathway context in this dataset. They are not interaction tests, so they do not prove equivalence between strata or absence of causal modification; however, the estimates are far from the clinical threshold and are consistent with previously validated main effects, so multiplicity is less concerning here.

The replication-stress/MYC checks are more informative for scope. Direct MYC amplification versus dependency_WRN (H195) gives a tiny signed effect of +0.033, 95% signed interval +0.002 to +0.064. Although the signed direction is favorable to more negative WRN dependency, the interval lies below the +0.10 clinical benchmark, so the claim of a clinically meaningful MYC-WRN association is rejected. In contrast, MSI-high remains strongly associated with dependency_WRN among MYC-nonamplified cells (H196, lower +0.763), KEAP1-loss remains strongly associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2 among MYC-amplified cells (H197, lower +0.729), and PTEN-loss remains associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 among MYC-amplified cells (H198, lower +0.174). Thus the WRN effect is highly specific to MSI-high status rather than a broad MYC/replication-stress effect, and the KEAP1/NFE2L2 and PTEN/STAT3 associations remain clinically benchmarked in a MYC-amplified context.

The specificity checks also reject competing broad associations. BRCA2 loss is not clinically meaningfully associated with dependency_WRN in MSI-high-negative cells (H29, signed estimate +0.001, upper +0.032), supporting the view that the WRN association in this dataset is centered on MSI-high status rather than BRCA2 loss confounding. MYC amplification is not clinically meaningfully associated with dependency_SMARCA2 among SMARCA4-wildtype cells (H167, signed estimate +0.012, upper +0.014), supporting specificity of the SMARCA2 association for SMARCA4-loss context. These nulls do not prove exact zero or absence in all datasets; they indicate that, in this dataset, clinically meaningful effects are excluded by the 95% intervals at the chosen benchmark.

No independent validation is requested. The newly accepted claims are far from the +0.10 decision boundary or are supported by the same very large central effects already validated; the rejected claims are already bounded below the clinical benchmark, and validation of peripheral null or subgroup estimates would not materially change the central conclusions. The evidence continues to support within-dataset descriptive associations, not causality or external generalizability.

record.narrative:
H102 response deadline assessed: the PTEN-loss versus non-PTEN-loss contrast for dependency_STAT3 among TP53-loss cells is clinically meaningful and independently supported. Discovery R99 gave a signed mean difference of +0.190 with 95% interval +0.085 to +0.296, and independent validation R179 gave +0.298 with an independent interval +0.141 to +0.454. Because H102 has direction -1, positive signed estimates correspond to more negative dependency_STAT3 in PTEN-loss cells, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency, within the TP53-loss eligible subgroup. The validated lower bound is above the +0.10 clinically meaningful benchmark, so I accept H102 and keep the investigation closed. This strengthens the central PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in a TP53-loss context, but it remains a within-dataset association and not a causal claim.

Final scientific report: The dataset supports five central measured-predictor associations with scientifically meaningful differences in CRISPR dependency scores. MSI-high cells show much stronger dependency_WRN; SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger dependency_SMARCA2; KEAP1-loss cells show much weaker dependency_NFE2L2; TP53-loss cells show much weaker dependency_USP7; and PTEN-loss cells show stronger dependency_STAT3. The central effect sizes are very large for MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, with signed effects near +0.78 to +0.81 and validated intervals far above +0.10. TP53-loss/USP7 is a robust moderate effect near +0.38 to +0.40 with validated support. PTEN-loss/STAT3 is a robust moderate effect near +0.27 to +0.33 with validated support, and the TP53-loss-stratified estimate now has independent validation at +0.298 with lower bound +0.141.

The central conclusions are not limited to one screen library, lineage subtype, QC subset, batch, mutation-burden band, or PIK3CA stratum. The PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect is clinically benchmarked in PIK3CA-wildtype and PIK3CA-mutant cells, TP53-wildtype and TP53-loss cells, KRAS-wildtype and KRAS-mutant cells, MYC-amplified cells, CDKN2A-loss contexts, KEAP1-loss contexts, and MTAP-loss contexts. The SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect remains large across Avana and KY libraries, batch contexts, TP53 and CDKN2A contexts, PIK3CA strata, ARID1A-loss contexts, MYC-stratified checks, and SMARCA4-loss specificity checks. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 effect is strong in PIK3CA strata, MYC-amplified cells, TP53-loss and TP53-wildtype cells, ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-wildtype contexts, and MSI-negative cells. The TP53-loss/USP7 effect is robust across PIK3CA strata, CDKN2A contexts, KEAP1 strata, ARID1A contexts, PIK3CA strata, Avana and validated KY contexts, and mutation-burden bands; interaction by mutation burden is not clinically meaningful after validation.

Negative findings are substantial. The data do not support clinically meaningful oncotarget-concordant dependencies for several canonical predictors: KRAS mutation is not meaningfully associated with stronger dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification is not meaningfully associated with dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification is not meaningfully associated with dependency_ERBB2. MYC amplification does not show a clinically meaningful association with dependency_WRN, dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-wildtype cells, dependency_USP7, or most other tested dependencies, despite a small direction-consistent MYC/WRN effect below the benchmark. ARID1A loss is not a clinically meaningful independent predictor of dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-wildtype cells, and STK11 loss is not a meaningful independent predictor of dependency_NFE2L2 in KEAP1-wildtype cells. BRCA2 loss does not show a clinically meaningful association with dependency_WRN in MSI-high-negative cells, supporting specificity of the WRN association for MSI-high status rather than a broader DNA-damage-confounded signal. MTAP loss is not a clinically meaningful independent predictor of dependency_USP7 or dependency_MDM2. Research markers D, E, and F do not produce central clinically meaningful effects on the tested dependency scores.

Unresolved uncertainty remains. The analysis is association-level within this supplied dataset; it does not establish that these predictor changes cause dependency changes, nor does it establish external generalizability. Some effect-modification questions are not fully settled: interaction intervals for several co-occurring pathway contexts are wide or do not meet the +0.10 threshold, and the KY CRISPR-library PTEN-loss/STAT3 subgroup remains below the clinical benchmark even though the central PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect is accepted and validated. These subgroup-level unresolved items do not weaken the main within-dataset conclusions, but they prevent strong claims of equal effect size across all libraries or co-mutation strata.

Most informative next analysis: additional discovery of main effects is less valuable than targeted replication or multivariable assessment of effect modification among central pathway contexts. If only internal resources are used, the most informative next comparisons would pre-specify and validate interactions such as PTEN loss x TP53 loss for dependency_STAT3 and TP53 loss x KEAP1 loss for dependency_USP7, because the main effects are already robust but their co-occurrence interactions have wide uncertainty. Ideally, the next step would be an independent external validation cohort or an adjusted joint model that tests simultaneous co-mutations, rather than continuing to expand subgroup-specific Welch estimates.

Iteration 18/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I use this explore step to move from repeated main-effect robustness checks toward pre-specified co-mutation decomposition for the two most informative unresolved pathway interactions: TP53 loss x KEAP1 loss for dependency_USP7 and PTEN loss x TP53 loss for dependency_STAT3. The central associations are already accepted and independently validated: MSI-high with much stronger dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7, and PTEN loss with stronger dependency_STAT3. The remaining scientific question is whether these are independent effects, additive effects, redundant effects, or context-modified effects when central pathway lesions co-occur. I therefore register clean interaction tests and complementary conditional main effects for TP53/KEAP1 on USP7 and PTEN/TP53 on STAT3, using eligibility restrictions that exclude other central pathway contexts to make effect modification more interpretable. For USP7, positive signed effects indicate weaker USP7 dependency; for STAT3, negative raw effects or positive signed effects under direction -1 indicate stronger STAT3 dependency. I also register central context checks that were not fully covered: PTEN/STAT3 in SMARCA4-loss cells, TP53/USP7 in MSI-high cells, KEAP1/NFE2L2 in MSI-high cells, SMARCA4/SMARCA2 in MYC-amplified cells, and KEAP1/USP7 in TP53-loss cells. Finally, a specificity test asks whether KEAP1 loss has a clinically meaningful association with dependency_WRN, which would challenge WRN association specificity. All comparisons use the same pre-specified benchmark: valid Welch cells with at least 20 observations per cell; a signed 95% lower bound above +0.10 supports a clinically meaningful association or interaction in the registered direction; an interval excluding +0.10 on the favorable side supports rejection; intervals crossing +0.10 remain unresolved. These are within-dataset association/effect-modification hypotheses, not causal claims or claims about external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No assessments are due at this analyze step, so I use the analysis capacity to test all 12 active registered comparisons H199-H210. These are pre-specified within-dataset co-mutation decomposition and specificity checks for the five accepted central associations: MSI-high with stronger dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss with stronger dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7, and PTEN loss with stronger dependency_STAT3. The selected analyses test whether central effects are modified by co-occurring pathway lesions and whether nearby candidate predictors can be excluded. H199-H201 decompose TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss effects on dependency_USP7 in a context excluding PTEN loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. H202-H204 decompose PTEN-loss effects on dependency_STAT3 in a context excluding KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. H205-H208 test remaining central-context robustness in SMARCA4-loss, MSI-high, and MYC-amplified strata. H209 tests KEAP1-loss effects on dependency_USP7 among TP53-loss cells, and H210 is a specificity test for KEAP1 loss on dependency_WRN. All estimates will be interpreted against the pre-specified signed 95% Welch benchmark: a signed lower bound above +0.10 supports a clinically meaningful effect in the registered direction, a signed upper bound below +0.10 supports rejection, intervals crossing +0.10 remain unresolved, and invalid or underpowered cells remain unresolved rather than evidence of null. I do not reassess accepted central claims now because no due evidence exists; any validation request will be considered only after these discovery results are appraised.

record.narrative: All 12 newly delivered discovery results are valid Welch comparisons and are judged against the pre-specified operational clinical benchmark: a signed 95% lower bound above +0.10 supports a clinically meaningful association or interaction in the registered direction, an interval whose upper bound is below +0.10 supports rejection, and an interval crossing +0.10 remains unresolved. H201 is accepted: TP53 loss gives a large weaker-dependency shift for dependency_USP7 in KEAP1-loss, non-PTEN-loss, non-SMARCA4-loss, non-MSI-high cells, signed estimate +0.466 with lower bound +0.280, well above threshold. H204 is accepted: PTEN loss gives a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency shift for dependency_STAT3 in clean TP53-wildtype, non-KEAP1-loss, non-SMARCA4-loss, non-MSI-high cells, lower bound +0.218. H205 is accepted: PTEN loss remains clinically meaningful among SMARCA4-loss cells, lower bound +0.118, supporting persistence of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in another co-mutation context. H207 is accepted: KEAP1 loss continues to give a very large weaker-dependency shift for dependency_NFE2L2 in MSI-high cells, lower bound +0.703. H208 is accepted: SMARCA4 loss continues to give a very large stronger-dependency shift for dependency_SMARCA2 in MYC-amplified cells, lower bound +0.759. These acceptances are far from the decision boundary except H205, and they reinforce central conclusions rather than create new peripheral claims. H202 is rejected: the PTEN-loss x TP53-loss interaction on dependency_STAT3 has a negative signed estimate in the registered direction and an upper bound of only +0.055, so a clinically meaningful favorable interaction is excluded, though this is a within-dataset effect-modification test and not a causal statement. H210 is rejected: KEAP1 loss is not clinically meaningfully associated with dependency_WRN, upper bound +0.037, which supports WRN specificity for MSI-high status. I use this explore step to move from repeated main-effect robustness checks toward pre-specified co-mutation decomposition for the two most informative unresolved pathway interactions: TP53 loss x KEAP1 loss for dependency_USP7 and PTEN loss x TP53 loss for dependency_STAT3. The central associations are already accepted and independently validated: MSI-high with much stronger dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7, and PTEN loss with stronger dependency_STAT3. The remaining scientific question is whether these are independent effects, additive effects, redundant effects, or context-modified effects when central pathway lesions co-occur. I therefore register clean interaction tests and complementary conditional main effects for TP53/KEAP1 on USP7 and PTEN/TP53 on STAT3, using eligibility restrictions that exclude other central pathway contexts to make effect modification more interpretable. For USP7, positive signed effects indicate weaker USP7 dependency; for STAT3, negative raw effects or positive signed effects under direction -1 indicate stronger STAT3 dependency. I also register central context checks that were not fully covered: PTEN/STAT3 in SMARCA4-loss cells, TP53/USP7 in MSI-high cells, KEAP1/NFE2L2 in MSI-high cells, SMARCA4/SMARCA2 in MYC-amplified cells, and KEAP1/USP7 in TP53-loss cells. record.narrative:
In this synthesis I assessed the new validation for H203, the PTEN-loss versus non-PTEN-loss contrast for dependency_STAT3 in cells with TP53 loss that also lack KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. Because H203 has direction -1, a positive signed estimate means more negative dependency_STAT3 in PTEN-loss cells, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency. The signed validation estimate is +0.206, direction-consistent with stronger STAT3 dependency, but the independent validation interval is -0.055 to +0.467. The lower bound is below zero and below the +0.10 clinically meaningful benchmark used throughout this run. The exposed cell contains only 30 samples, so the strict co-mutation context is underpowered. I therefore keep H203 unresolved and close further investigation: the data do not establish a clinically meaningful PTEN-loss effect in this narrow TP53-loss/non-KEAP1-loss/non-SMARCA4-loss/non-MSI-high context, but they also do not exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect.

This does not undermine the central PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 association. The broad PTEN-loss effect is accepted and independently validated, with signed estimates near +0.27 to +0.33 and validated lower bounds above +0.25 in H93, H102, and several stratum checks. H203 shows that the narrowest clean co-mutation context remains uncertain, while H204 supports a clinically meaningful PTEN-loss effect in TP53-wildtype clean contexts and H102 supports a meaningful effect among TP53-loss cells without the additional KEAP1/SMARCA4/MSI restrictions.

Final scientific report. Within this supplied lung cancer dependency dataset, five central measured associations are supported as scientifically meaningful under the pre-specified absolute dependency-score shift benchmark of +0.10 or greater. First, MSI-high status is associated with very strong dependency_WRN, signed effect approximately +0.79, with independent validation at +0.80 and an independent lower bound well above the benchmark. This is specific: BRCA2 loss does not show a clinically meaningful WRN effect among MSI-negative cells, and KEAP1 loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_WRN. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with very strong dependency_SMARCA2, signed effect approximately +0.78, with independent validation and robustness across libraries, lineages, batches, QC subsets, mutation-burden bands, PIK3CA strata, TP53/CDKN2A/KEAP1/ARID1A/MYC contexts, and SMARCA4-loss contexts. ARID1A loss alone is not a meaningful predictor of dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-wildtype cells, supporting specificity. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with very weak dependency_NFE2L2, signed effect approximately +0.80, with independent validation and robustness across TP53, PIK3CA, MYC, ARID1A, STK11, MSI, library, and QC contexts. STK11 loss alone is not a meaningful predictor of dependency_NFE2L2 in KEAP1-wildtype cells. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_USP7, signed effect approximately +0.39, with independent validation and robustness across PIK3CA, CDKN2A, STK11, MTAP, KEAP1, ARID1A, MSI-negative, library, QC, and mutation-burden contexts; mutation-burden interaction did not survive validation. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, signed effect approximately +0.30, with independent validation and robustness across PIK3CA, TP53, KRAS, MYC, KEAP1, ARID1A, MTAP, mutation-burden, QC, and co-mutation-restricted TP53-wildtype contexts.

The run also yields many important negative findings. The data do not support clinically meaningful oncotarget-concordant dependency for several canonical predictor-target pairs: KRAS mutation is not meaningfully associated with dependency_KRAS; BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with dependency_BRAF; EGFR amplification is not meaningfully associated with dependency_EGFR; ERBB2 amplification is not meaningfully associated with dependency_ERBB2. MYC amplification is not a meaningful predictor for most dependencies tested, including dependency_WRN, dependency_MDM2, dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, dependency_DHX9, dependency_TMED10, dependency_STAT3 in PTEN-wildtype cells, dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-wildtype cells, and dependency_USP7. ARID1A loss is not a meaningful independent predictor of dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-wildtype cells. STK11 loss is not meaningful for dependency_NFE2L2 in KEAP1-wildtype cells. MTAP loss is not meaningful for dependency_USP7 or dependency_MDM2 independently of TP53 loss. Research markers D, E, and F do not produce central clinically meaningful dependency effects. PTEN-loss interaction with TP53 loss for dependency_STAT3 was not favorable enough to support clinically meaningful interaction, and KEAP1 loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_WRN, supporting WRN specificity for MSI-high status.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly at the level of co-mutation decomposition and library/subgroup heterogeneity. Several interaction intervals for central pathway contexts are wide or do not cross the +0.10 benchmark, including PTEN-loss effects in the narrow TP53-loss/non-KEAP1-loss/non-SMARCA4-loss/non-MSI-high stratum, PTEN-loss effects in the KY CRISPR-library subgroup, KEAP1-loss effects on dependency_USP7 in TP53-loss cells, TP53-loss effects on dependency_USP7 in MSI-high cells, and several mutation-burden or ARID1A effect-modification checks. These unresolved items are not evidence of null; they mostly reflect small exposed cells and wide independent intervals. The central associations themselves are supported independently of these narrow subgroup tests. The conclusions are within-dataset associations. They do not establish causality, therapeutic sufficiency, or external generalizability.

Most informative next analysis: stop expanding subgroup Welch comparisons. The most valuable next step is either external replication in an independent cohort or an adjusted joint model that simultaneously evaluates MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, and PTEN loss, with appropriate interaction tests for co-occurring pathway lesions. If using only this dataset, the highest-yield targets would be pre-specified multivariable interaction models for PTEN loss x TP53 loss on dependency_STAT3 and TP53 loss x KEAP1 loss on dependency_USP7, because the main effects are robust but the co-occurrence effects are underpowered in single Welch subgroup contrasts.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so this explore step adds pre-specified, high-value follow-up hypotheses rather than revisiting already resolved claims. No validation requests remain in the run, so the goal is to use the remaining discovery capacity for two focused scientific questions. First, I test whether the four accepted central associations persist in cells lacking the other four central pathway lesions: KEAP1 loss with dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with dependency_USP7, SMARCA4 loss with dependency_SMARCA2, and MSI-high status with dependency_WRN. These clean-context contrasts are proxies for an adjusted joint model: a signed estimate at or above the run's +0.10 benchmark would support that the central effect is not merely carried by co-occurring accepted pathway lesions, whereas an interval crossing +0.10 would leave independence unresolved and an upper bound below +0.10 would be evidence against a meaningful effect in the registered direction. Second, I test whether PTEN loss, which is already robustly associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, extends to other PI3K/AKT/mTOR-linked dependency outcomes. I expect PTEN loss to be associated with stronger dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, and, in TP53-wildtype cells, dependency_MDM2, because PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling, which can support proliferative transcription, translation, and MDM2-mediated p53 suppression. The plausible alternatives are no clinically meaningful PI3K-linked effect or an effect in the opposite direction. I also test two canonical MDM2-axis hypotheses in TP53-wildtype cells: MYC amplification may be associated with stronger MDM2 dependency through MYC-p14ARF-MDM2 stress signaling, while CDKN2A/p14ARF loss may be associated with weaker MDM2 dependency because p14ARF loss alters MDM2-mediated p53 control. Finally, I test whether SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency_POLR2A, which would expand the SWI/SNF synthetic-lethality result beyond SMARCA2; failure to cross the benchmark would support SMARCA2 specificity. All proposals remain within-dataset association hypotheses and do not imply causality or external generalizability.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

status (accept/reject/unresolved),

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The new batch mostly supports the central dependency associations in co-mutation-restricted contexts and rejects the extension hypotheses. Using the run's pre-specified signed +0.10 dependency-score benchmark as the conservative clinical-significance analogue for these standardized scores, H212, H213, and H214 are accepted: TP53 loss remains strongly associated with weaker dependency_USP7 in clean non-KEAP1/non-PTEN/non-SMARCA4/non-MSI contexts (signed estimate +0.409, lower +0.310); SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with stronger dependency_SMARCA2 in clean TP53/KEAP1/PTEN/MSI-negative contexts (+0.791, lower +0.764); and MSI-high status remains strongly associated with stronger dependency_WRN in clean TP53/KEAP1/PTEN/SMARCA4-negative contexts (+0.774, lower +0.728). These lower bounds are far above the benchmark, so residual confounding by the excluded central pathway lesions cannot plausibly explain them away. H215-H218, H220 are rejected because all upper bounds are far below +0.10: PTEN loss does not meaningfully extend to dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, or TP53-wildtype dependency_MDM2; MYC amplification does not meaningfully extend to TP53-wildtype dependency_MDM2; and SMARCA4 loss does not meaningfully extend to dependency_POLR2A. H219 is rejected for the registered CDKN2A-loss-to-stronger-MDM2-dependency direction: the signed estimate is negative, and although the raw opposite shift has a point magnitude above the benchmark, its signed lower bound after reversal is about 0.079, which does not clear the +0.10 benchmark; it is therefore not accepted as a clinically meaningful pre-specified association. H211 has a coding/eligibility contradiction: the exposure is keap1_loss but the displayed eligibility requires keap1_loss=0, which would leave no exposed cells, while the returned valid cell_n indicates either the intended analysis was not exactly the registered claim or the eligibility was not applied. Because I cannot verify which analysis generated R217, I keep H211 unresolved and close it as a clean-context test, while registering a corrected parent-linked clean KEAP1/NFE2L2 proposal for possible follow-up. I expect PTEN loss to be associated with stronger dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, and, in TP53-wildtype cells, dependency_MDM2, because PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling, which can support proliferative transcription, translation, and MDM2-mediated p53 suppression. The plausible alternatives are no clinically meaningful PI3K-linked effect or an effect in the opposite direction. I also test two canonical MDM2-axis hypotheses in TP53-wildtype cells: MYC amplification may be associated with stronger MDM2 dependency through MYC-p14ARF-MDM2 stress signaling, while CDKN2A/p14ARF loss may be associated with weaker MDM2 dependency because p14ARF loss alters MDM2-mediated p53 control. No validation is requested because none remain.","synthesize":"In this synthesis I assessed the new validation for H203, the PTEN-loss versus non-PTEN-loss contrast for dependency_STAT3 in cells with TP53 loss that also lack KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. Because H203 has direction -1, a positive signed estimate means more negative dependency_STAT3 in PTEN-loss cells, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency. The signed validation estimate is +0.206, direction-consistent with stronger STAT3 dependency, but the independent validation interval is -0.055 to +0.467. The lower bound is below zero and below the +0.10 clinically meaningful benchmark used throughout this run. The exposed cell contains only 30 samples, so the strict co-mutation context is underpowered. I therefore keep H203 unresolved and close further investigation: the data do not establish a clinically meaningful PTEN-loss effect in this narrow TP53-loss/non-KEAP1-loss/non-SMARCA4-loss/non-MSI-high context, but they also do not exclude a clinically meaningful positive effect.\n\nThis does not undermine the central PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 association. The broad PTEN-loss effect is accepted and independently validated, with signed estimates near +0.27 to +0.33 and validated lower bounds above +0.25 in H93, H102, and several stratum checks. H203 shows that the narrowest clean co-mutation context remains uncertain, while H204 supports a clinically meaningful PTEN-loss effect in TP53-wildtype clean contexts and H102 supports a meaningful effect among TP53-loss cells without the additional KEAP1/SMARCA4/MSI restrictions.\n\nFinal scientific report. Within this supplied lung cancer dependency dataset, five central measured associations are supported as scientifically meaningful under the pre-specified absolute dependency-score shift benchmark of +0.10 or greater. First, MSI-high status is associated with very strong dependency_WRN, signed effect approximately +0.79, with independent validation at +0.80 and an independent lower bound well above the benchmark. This is specific: BRCA2 loss does not show a clinically meaningful WRN effect among MSI-negative cells, and KEAP1 loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_WRN. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with very strong dependency_SMARCA2, signed effect approximately +0.78, with independent validation and robustness across libraries, lineages, batches, QC subsets, mutation-burden bands, PIK3CA strata, TP53/CDKN2A/KEAP1/ARID1A/MYC contexts, and SMARCA4-loss contexts. ARID1A loss alone is not a meaningful predictor of dependency_SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-wildtype cells, supporting specificity. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with very weak dependency_NFE2L2, signed effect approximately +0.80, with independent validation and robustness across TP53, PIK3CA, MYC, ARID1A, STK11, MSI, library, and QC contexts. STK11 loss alone is not a meaningful predictor of dependency_NFE2L2 in KEAP1-wildtype cells. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_USP7, signed effect approximately +0.39, with independent validation and robustness across PIK3CA, CDKN2A, STK11, MTAP, KEAP1, ARID1A, MSI-negative, library, QC, and mutation-burden contexts; mutation-burden interaction did not survive validation. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, signed effect approximately +0.30, with independent validation and robustness across PIK3CA, TP53, KRAS, MYC, KEAP1, ARID1A, MTAP, mutation-burden, QC, and co-mutation-restricted TP53-wildtype contexts.\n\nThe run also yields many important negative findings. The data do not support clinically meaningful oncotarget-concordant dependency for several canonical predictor-target pairs: KRAS mutation is not meaningfully associated with dependency_KRAS; BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with dependency_BRAF; EGFR amplification is not meaningfully associated with dependency_EGFR; ERBB2 amplification is not meaningfully associated with dependency_ERBB2. record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no voluntary validation budget remains, so this explore step registers a focused batch of new discovery comparisons. The accepted central associations are robust, but the remaining scientific value lies less in repeating broad robustness checks and more in asking whether the accepted effects are modified by pathway partners or extend to nearby proliferation/translation/transcription dependencies. I pre-specify the same run-wide signed dependency-score benchmark: an accepted claim needs an estimate whose lower bound is at least +0.10 relative to the claim direction; an upper bound below +0.10 rejects clinically meaningful association in the registered direction; an interval crossing +0.10 remains unresolved. These are within-dataset association hypotheses, not causal or generalizability claims.

The interaction set tests biological crosstalk among PTEN loss/PI3K signaling, TP53 loss, KEAP1/oxidative stress, SMARCA4 chromatin remodeling, MSI status, and MYC amplification. For PTEN loss and dependency_STAT3, MYC amplification is the strongest pre-specified modifier because PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MYC can cooperate to drive proliferative and STAT3-linked transcriptional programs; raw interaction negative would mean the PTEN effect is stronger/more negative in MYC-amplified cells. I also test whether SWI/SNF loss or KEAP1 loss modifies the PTEN effect, with expected uncertainty because these pathways may act independently. For TP53 loss and dependency_USP7, I test SMARCA4 loss and MYC amplification as effect modifiers of the already accepted p53-USP7 association, expecting uncertain direction because USP7 is not MYC- or chromatin-specific in prior tests. For KEAP1 loss and dependency_NFE2L2, SMARCA4 loss is tested because oxidative stress can interact with chromatin/transcriptional stress responses, though the broad KEAP1 effect may remain additive. For SMARCA4 loss and dependency_SMARCA2, MYC amplification is a plausible potentiator if MYC-driven proliferation amplifies SWI/SNF synthetic lethality. For MSI-high and dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss tests whether DNA-repair deficiency and SWI/SNF dysfunction cooperate; the subgroup co-cell count is modest, so invalid or wide intervals are plausible.

The mean-difference set tests specificity and possible broader pathway effects. PTEN loss has already been shown not to extend to dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, or TP53-wildtype dependency_MDM2. I therefore test PTEN loss against two additional proliferation/translation-associated dependencies, dependency_KIF18A and dependency_DHX9, expecting raw negative associations if PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling supports stronger mitotic and RNA-helicase/translation-associated dependencies; failure to clear the +0.10 benchmark would strengthen the specificity of the PTEN-STAT3 result. KEAP1 loss against dependency_STAT3 tests whether oxidative-stress pathway lesions also create STAT3 dependency rather than being specific to NFE2L2. TP53 loss against dependency_NFE2L2 tests p53-NRF2 crosstalk: p53 can regulate oxidative-stress responses, so TP53 loss may weaken NFE2L2 dependency, but this remains a low-confidence hypothesis. Overall, these proposals prioritize remaining uncertainty around modifier biology and outcome specificity while avoiding further low-yield replication of already accepted central associations.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All newly delivered discovery results were assessed as within-dataset association tests using the pre-specified signed +0.10 dependency-score benchmark: accept only when the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10, reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.10, and leave unresolved when the interval crosses +0.10. No validation request is possible because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so no new claim is promoted from unresolved to accepted on the basis of these exploratory comparisons. H222 and H226 are the only remaining unresolved results from this batch. H222 tests whether MYC amplification modifies the PTEN-loss effect on dependency_STAT3; the signed interaction estimate is small at +0.031 and the interval -0.101 to +0.163 crosses both the +0.10 benchmark and the null, so the data do not support or exclude a clinically meaningful interaction. H226 tests whether MYC amplification modifies the TP53-loss effect on dependency_USP7; the signed estimate +0.134 is above the benchmark in point magnitude, but the interval -0.048 to +0.315 crosses the benchmark and the null, so the positive trend is too imprecise and too many multiplicity comparisons were run to accept. I close both as unresolved because they are small-cell, low-priority subgroup interactions and no validation remains. The other interaction tests are rejected because their signed upper bounds fall below +0.10: H223 PTEN-loss by SMARCA4-loss on STAT3, H225 TP53-loss by SMARCA4-loss on USP7, H227 KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss on NFE2L2, H228 SMARCA4-loss by MYC-amplification on SMARCA2, and H229 MSI-high by SMARCA4-loss on WRN. H229 is near the boundary, with signed upper bound 0.0975 and only 29 exposed cells in the subgroup cell, so it is close to the threshold but still fails the pre-specified benchmark; it should not be described as evidence for interaction. The specificity tests are also rejected under the same rule: H230 PTEN-loss does not meaningfully extend to dependency_KIF18A, H231 PTEN-loss does not meaningfully extend to dependency_DHX9, H232 KEAP1-loss does not meaningfully extend to dependency_STAT3, and H233 TP53-loss does not meaningfully extend to dependency_NFE2L2. H52 closes the ERBB2 oncotarget-specificity question by rejecting a meaningful ERBB2-amplification effect on dependency_ERBB2 even among TP53-wildtype cells. From a critical-review perspective, these comparisons are internally clean: exposures are measured genotypes or markers, outcomes are pre-specified dependency scores, and no outcome information is used as an exposure or eligibility variable. The main limitations are multiplicity, small subgroup cell counts in some interaction cells, and absence of independent validation. Therefore, none of these new results changes the accepted central associations. They strengthen outcome specificity for PTEN/STAT3, KEAP1/NFE2L2, TP53/USP7, MSI/WRN, and SMARCA4/SMARCA2, while providing no robust evidence for MYC, SMARCA4, KEAP1, TP53, or MSI effect modification in the tested pairings and no evidence that PTEN extends to KIF18A or DHX9.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

The prior run established five central within-dataset associations: MSI-high/stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4-loss/stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency, TP53-loss/weaker USP7 dependency, and PTEN-loss/stronger STAT3 dependency. The main remaining scientific gaps are (1) whether TP53 loss has an independent main effect on STAT3 dependency, because TP53 loss has been tested mainly as a modifier or co-stratifier rather than as the exposure of interest; (2) whether SWI/SNF dysfunction has dependency effects beyond SMARCA2, especially on WRN in MSI-negative cells, to test whether SMARCA4 loss reflects a broader DNA-repair/replication-stress vulnerability; (3) whether KEAP1 loss affects USP7 outside its TP53-loss and TP53-wildtype conditional tests, completing a central predictor-outcome pair; and (4) whether receptor tyrosine kinase or LKB1 pathway lesions associate with STAT3 dependency rather than only with their nominal target dependencies. The clean co-wildtype stratum removes PTEN loss, KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, and SMARCA4 loss to reduce confounding by other accepted predictors. For SMARCA4 loss and WRN, I also hypothesize negative raw contrasts, with the MSI-negative stratum testing specificity apart from the dominant MSI-high effect. For KEAP1 loss and USP7, direction is set positive because the prior TP53-loss association was in the weaker-USP7 direction, but the mechanistic expectation is weak, so anticipated_direction is uncertain. For EGFR and ERBB2 amplification with STAT3, the expectation is negative raw contrasts because upstream receptor signaling could cooperate with STAT3-linked proliferation or survival programs even when these lesions do not show concordant oncotarget dependency. expectation

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All ten newly delivered discovery results are valid Welch comparisons and internally clean: exposures are measured genotype or marker variables, outcomes are pre-specified CRISPR dependency scores, and no outcome information is used as exposure or eligibility. Using the run's pre-specified signed +0.10 dependency-score benchmark, none of the new results supports a clinically meaningful association in the registered direction: every signed 95% Welch interval has an upper bound below +0.10. H234 and H235 show no meaningful TP53-loss association with dependency_STAT3 overall or in the clean co-wildtype stratum. H236 shows no meaningful main KEAP1-loss association with dependency_USP7. H237 and H238 show no meaningful SMARCA4-loss association with dependency_WRN overall or specifically among MSI-negative cells. H239-H241 show no meaningful EGFR-amplification, ERBB2-amplification, or STK11-loss association with dependency_STAT3. H30 is of particular note: among KRAS-WT cells, NF1 loss has a signed interval entirely below zero, but the magnitude is small and opposite the tested direction, so it is rejected as a positive meaningful KRAS-dependency effect; it does not meet the benchmark for a reversed effect either. H69 shows only a weak positive trend for EGFR amplification among STK11-WT cells on dependency_EGFR, with an upper bound well below +0.10. With validation budget exhausted, these rejections are within-dataset conclusions: they strengthen outcome specificity for the accepted central associations, especially PTEN-loss/STAT3, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, TP53-loss/USP7, MSI-high/WRN, and SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, but they do not prove absence in larger or independent samples.

Independent validation R216 gave signed estimate +0.206 but independent interval -0.055 to +0.467 with only 30 exposed cells. The point estimate is directionally supportive, but the interval both fails to clear +0.10 and includes zero, so the independent validation neither confirms nor excludes a clinically meaningful narrow-stratum effect. I therefore keep H203 unresolved and closed: no validation budget remains, and the small exposed cell makes this residual contrast too imprecise to support. This does not weaken the broad accepted PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 association, which remains accepted and independently validated. \n\nSupported findings in the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset, using the run-pre-specified signed +0.10 dependency-score benchmark and recognizing these are associations only, are five central predictor-dependency relationships. First, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger dependency_WRN: broad discovery signed estimate about +0.79 to +0.80, independent validation +0.802 with lower bound +0.753 (R52), and robustness across TP53-wildtype, library, lineage, mutation-burden, co-mutation-negative, and other strata. Outcome specificity is supported by null BRCA2-loss contrasts among MSI-negative cells and by null KEAP1-loss effects on WRN overall. \n\nSecond, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2: broad discovery estimate about +0.78, independent validation +0.793 with lower bound +0.763 (R13), and robustness across CRISPR libraries, batches, lineage subtypes, QC subsets, mutation-burden bands, PIK3CA strata, and co-mutation-restricted contexts. ARID1A loss is not a meaningful independent predictor in SMARCA4-wildtype cells, supporting specificity for SMARCA4 rather than generic SWI/SNF loss. \n\nThird, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2, i.e. less negative dependency scores: broad signed estimate about +0.80, independent validation about +0.807 with lower bound +0.775, and a clean TP53-wildtype, PTEN-nonloss, SMARCA4-nonloss, MSI-negative contrast accepted under the benchmark. STK11 loss does not meaningfully predict dependency_NFE2L2 among KEAP1-wildtype cells, supporting pathway specificity. \n\nFourth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7: broad discovery estimate about +0.396, independent validation about +0.395 with lower bound +0.293, robust across many genotypic and assay contexts including PIK3CA, CDKN2A, STK11, MTAP, KEAP1, ARID1A, MSI-negative, library, QC, and clean co-mutation-negative settings. A high mutation-burden interaction did not survive validation, so mutation-burden effect modification remains unsupported. \n\nFifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, i.e. more negative dependency scores: broad discovery estimate about +0.27, independent validation about +0.329 with lower bound +0.255, and robustness across PIK3CA, TP53, KRAS, MYC, KEAP1, ARID1A, MTAP, mutation-burden, QC, and broader co-mutation-restricted contexts. Only the narrow TP53-loss, KEAP1-nonloss, SMARCA4-nonloss, MSI-negative stratum remains unresolved because of small sample size. \n\nNegative findings are scientifically informative. record.narrative: Assessment of H203 and final synthesis. H203 tested PTEN loss versus PTEN wild type for dependency_STAT3 within TP53-loss cells lacking KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. Discovery R208 signed estimate +0.186, interval +0.039 to +0.333, so the point estimate is directionally supportive but the lower bound is below the pre-specified +0.10 meaningfulness benchmark. Independent validation R216 signed estimate +0.206, independent interval -0.055 to +0.467, with only 30 exposed cells. The validation point estimate is consistent, but it neither excludes a clinically meaningful effect nor clears the benchmark. I therefore keep H203 unresolved and close it because no validation budget remains and the narrow contrast is too imprecise. This does not weaken the broad accepted PTEN-loss and dependency_STAT3 association, which was accepted and independently validated in larger comparisons. Final report: In the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset, five central within-dataset associations are supported under the signed +0.10 benchmark. MSI-high status is associated with much stronger dependency_WRN, R6 discovery about +0.79 and R52 validation +0.802 lower +0.753, robust across TP53 wild type, libraries, lineage, mutation-burden bands, co-mutation-negative strata, and other contexts. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2, R8 discovery about +0.78 and R13 validation +0.793 lower +0.763, robust across libraries, batches, lineage subtypes, QC subsets, mutation-burden bands, PIK3CA strata, and co-mutation restrictions; ARID1A loss is not meaningful in SMARCA4 wild type cells, supporting specificity. KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2, i.e. less negative scores, R20 and R39 signed effect about +0.80 lower +0.775, with clean multi-negative strata accepted and STK11 loss null among KEAP1 wild type cells. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7, R15 and R17 discovery about +0.396 and R26 validation about +0.395 lower +0.293, robust across genotypic and assay contexts; the high mutation-burden interaction did not survive validation, R153, so mutation-burden modification is unsupported. PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, R93 discovery about +0.27 and R90 validation about +0.329 lower +0.255, robust across PIK3CA, TP53, KRAS, MYC, KEAP1, ARID1A, MTAP, mutation-burden, QC, and co-mutation-restricted contexts. Negative findings are informative: canonical oncogene-concordant dependency is not supported, KRAS mutation does not meaningfully predict dependency_KRAS R1, BRAF V600E does not predict dependency_BRAF R3, EGFR amplification does not predict dependency_EGFR R4, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict dependency_ERBB2 R5, including TP53 wild type and STK11 wild type subsets. TP53 loss does not meaningfully predict dependency_MDM2 R7 or dependency_STAT3 R239, and MYC amplification is not clinically meaningful across most tested dependencies. MTAP loss is not independently meaningful for dependency_USP7 or dependency_MDM2 outside TP53-loss context. PTEN loss does not extend meaningfully to dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, TP53 wild type dependency_MDM2, dependency_KIF18A, or dependency_DHX9. KEAP1 loss is not meaningfully associated with dependency_WRN or dependency_STAT3, and MSI-high is not meaningfully associated with dependency_DHX9. Research markers D, E, and F do not show central clinically meaningful dependency effects. Many pre-specified interactions are rejected as not clearing +0.10, including PTEN-loss by SMARCA4-loss for dependency_STAT3, TP53-loss by SMARCA4-loss for dependency_USP7, KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss for dependency_NFE2L2, SMARCA4-loss by MYC-amplification for dependency_SMARCA2, and MSI-high by SMARCA4-loss for dependency_WRN. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score).
