Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so this explore step registers new discovery-only comparisons rather than repeating validated or closed contrasts. The existing accepted within-dataset associations remain the scientific anchors: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The new proposals test scientifically meaningful complementary questions: whether receptor tyrosine kinase amplification creates cross-family dependency, whether PI3K pathway mutation reduces upstream ERBB2 dependency after excluding EGFR and ERBB2 amplification, whether replication-stress-associated lesions RB1 loss, MTAP loss, and STK11 loss predict stronger WRN dependency specifically among MSI-negative cells to avoid confounding by the dominant MSI-high effect, whether APC mutation associates with STAT3 dependency in PTEN wild type cells, whether TP53 loss predicts weaker RPL11 or KIF18A dependency through altered p53-dependent stress and checkpoint programs, whether KEAP1 loss has an independent chromatin-remodeling association with SMARCA2, whether BRAF V600E among KRAS wild type cells shows weaker KRAS dependency because BRAF lies downstream, and whether PTEN loss among TP53 wild type cells has an independent USP7 association. For dependency scores, more negative values mean stronger dependency. A negative anticipated raw contrast therefore means stronger dependency in exposed versus comparator, while a positive anticipated raw contrast means weaker dependency. Each claim will be judged with the pre-specified signed +0.10 benchmark: accept when the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10, reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.10, and leave unresolved when the interval crosses the benchmark or when cell counts are invalid. These are exploratory association hypotheses in the supplied dataset only, not causal claims, and null results would strengthen outcome specificity while accepted results would require external replication.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so the analyze step now serves the final discovery sweep rather than validation or reassessment. I select exactly the 12 active, still-untested claims H242-H253. This allocation is scientifically efficient because these claims test specificity and mechanistic complementarity around the five accepted central associations: MSI-high/dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss/dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss/dependency_USP7, and PTEN loss/dependency_STAT3. The selected claims cover three useful areas: (1) RTK/pathway specificity and cross-family associations, including EGFR amplification with dependency_ERBB2 (H242), ERBB2 amplification with dependency_EGFR (H243), and PIK3CA mutation with dependency_ERBB2 among EGFR/ERBB2-amplification-negative cells (H244); (2) WRN-dependency specificity beyond the dominant MSI-high effect, by testing RB1 loss (H245), MTAP loss (H246), and STK11 loss (H247) only among MSI-negative cells; and (3) specificity or pathway-hierarchy checks for the accepted markers, including APC mutation with dependency_STAT3 among PTEN-wild-type cells (H248), TP53 loss with dependency_RPL11 and dependency_KIF18A (H249 and H250), KEAP1 loss with dependency_SMARCA2 (H251), BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type cells with dependency_KRAS (H252), and PTEN loss among TP53-wild-type cells with dependency_USP7 (H253). Each returned estimate and interval will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction. I will interpret them using the pre-specified dependency-score meaningfulness benchmark: accept when the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10, reject when the signed 95% Welch upper bound is below +0.10, and leave unresolved when the interval crosses +0.10 or when cell counts are invalid. Because validation budget is exhausted, any accepted new result would remain a within-dataset association and would not establish causality or external generalizability. Null results should still be recorded as informative for outcome and predictor specificity, particularly when they show that the central effects do not mechanically extend to nearby outcomes or nearby genotypes.

Iteration 22/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered discovery results are valid Welch comparisons with adequate cell counts and no apparent leakage: exposures are measured binary genotypes/markers, eligibility uses measured covariates only, and outcomes are the pre-specified CRISPR dependency scores. I retained the run's pre-specified signed +0.10 dependency-score benchmark: a claim is accepted only if the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10; otherwise it is rejected if the signed upper bound is below +0.10, and unresolved if it crosses the benchmark. Every due estimate has signed upper bound below +0.10, so none meets the prespecified clinically/scientifically meaningful threshold in the registered direction. H242-H243 reject cross-family receptor tyrosine kinase dependency effects: EGFR amplification does not meaningfully strengthen ERBB2 dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not meaningfully strengthen EGFR dependency. H244 rejects a PIK3CA-mutation effect on ERBB2 dependency after excluding EGFR and ERBB2 amplification. H245-H247 reject replication-stress lesion associations with WRN dependency among MSI-negative cells: RB1 loss, MTAP loss, and STK11 loss each have intervals incompatible with the required +0.10 effect, supporting outcome specificity of the accepted MSI-high/WRN association. H248 rejects APC mutation as a meaningful positive predictor of dependency_STAT3 among PTEN-wild-type cells. H249 rejects TP53 loss as a meaningful weaker dependency marker for RPL11. H250 is notable because its signed interval for TP53 loss and dependency_KIF18A is statistically nonzero in the opposite direction, but its magnitude is tiny (about -0.021, signed upper bound -0.001) and far below the +0.10 benchmark; it is rejected as not a clinically meaningful reversed association and I did not register a reversed claim. H251 rejects KEAP1 loss as an independent marker of dependency_SMARCA2. H252 rejects BRAF V600E as a meaningful predictor of dependency_KRAS among KRAS-wild-type cells. H253 rejects PTEN loss as a meaningful predictor of dependency_USP7 among TP53-wild-type cells. Collectively, these null results strengthen the specificity of the central accepted associations: MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, TP53-loss/USP7, and PTEN-loss/STAT3. They are within-dataset associations only and do not establish causality or generalizability. No validation was requested because the validation budget is exhausted. I registered a small final negative-control panel for MSI-high on KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, and STAT3, plus one refinement test of PTEN loss on dependency_STAT3 within ARID1A-loss cells, to add either outcome-specific null evidence or robustness evidence for the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association.

record.narrative: Final synthesis: no additional response deadlines are listed and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. I reassessed H203 using its discovery evidence R208 and validation evidence R216. R208 was directionally supportive but did not clear the pre-specified signed +0.10 meaningfulness benchmark in the supplied dataset, with signed estimate +0.186 and 95% interval +0.039 to +0.333. Independent validation R216 gave a similar point estimate, signed estimate +0.206, but the independent interval crossed both null and the +0.10 benchmark, +0.206 with interval -0.055 to +0.467, and it was based on only 30 exposed cells in the narrow stratum. I therefore keep H203 unresolved and closed. This is a precision problem in a small highly restricted contrast, not evidence against the broader accepted PTEN-loss and dependency_STAT3 association, which was independently validated in much larger comparisons. The overall report is that the supplied 2000-sample lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset supports five large within-dataset associations under the signed +0.10 practical-significance benchmark, while most other predictor-dependency links and interactions are null, small, inconsistent, or too imprecise. First, MSI-high status is strongly associated with more negative dependency_WRN. Discovery R6 gave +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819, and validation R52 gave +0.802 with interval +0.753 to +0.851. The effect is far above the +0.10 threshold and remained supported in multiple refinement contexts, including TP53-wild-type, Avana library, adenocarcinoma, batch A, high-quality RNA/DNA/CRISPR QC, different mutation-burden bands, and several co-mutation-restricted strata. The magnitude and robustness are striking, but this remains an association in this dataset, not proof that MSI status mechanistically causes WRN dependency. Second, SMARCA4 loss is strongly associated with more negative dependency_SMARCA2. Discovery R8 gave +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803, and validation R13 gave +0.793 with interval +0.763 to +0.822. Subgroup refinements across batch A, Avana, KY, adenocarcinoma, QC-restricted, PIK3CA strata, TP53, STK11, CDKN2A, KEAP1, ARID1A, MYC, and multi-negative co-mutation contexts were consistently supportive. By contrast, ARID1A loss did not show a meaningful SMARCA2 association within SMARCA4-wild-type cells, and the ARID1A interaction was null, supporting specificity for SMARCA4 rather than a general chromatin-remodeling loss effect. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2, i.e. less negative dependency scores. H20 accepted this signed positive direction using discovery R20 +0.796 with interval +0.776 to +0.816 and validation R39 +0.806 with interval +0.775 to +0.838. The opposite H9 direction was rejected. This finding is internally consistent across assay, lineage, mutation-burden, co-mutation, and library subsets, although the broader biological interpretation of KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 dependency remains uncertain. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. H15 accepted discovery R17 +0.396 with interval +0.325 to +0.467, and validation R26 was nearly identical, +0.395 with interval +0.293 to +0.498. Multiple refinement strata across library, TP53-cooccurring genotypes, QC, lineage, mutation burden, STK11, CDKN2A, ARID1A, KEAP1, PIK3CA, MYC, MTAP, and co-mutation-negative backgrounds were supportive. The only notable caution is the mutation-burden interaction: the discovery interaction H148 did not provide robust validation, R153 was negative and crossed the benchmark, so I do not support a meaningful TP53-loss by high mutation-burden modification of the USP7 association. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with more negative dependency_STAT3. H93 accepted discovery R88 +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319 and validation R90 +0.329 with interval +0.255 to +0.402. This association was supported in broad, TP53, KRAS, PIK3CA, MYC, KEAP1, ARID1A, MTAP, mutation-burden, QC, batch A, co-mutation-restricted, and multi-negative strata, and validation of some strata such as H102 R179 reinforced the main association. The narrow H203 stratum and the KY-library PTEN-loss stratum H96 remained unresolved because intervals crossed the +0.10 threshold, but these small precision issues do not overturn the broad validated PTEN-loss and STAT3 dependency association. The most important negative and specificity findings are as informative as the accepted associations. Canonical oncogene-concordant dependency was generally not supported: KRAS mutation did not meaningfully predict dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E did not predict dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification did not predict dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification did not predict dependency_ERBB2. Cross-family RTK checks also rejected EGFR amplification as a predictor of dependency_ERBB2 and ERBB2 amplification as a predictor of dependency_EGFR. PIK3CA mutation did not meaningfully predict dependency_ERBB2 after excluding EGFR and ERBB2 amplification. MYC amplification was not clinically meaningful across most tested dependency outcomes, although one tiny opposite-sign WRN contrast appeared; it was far below +0.10 and was not promoted. MTAP loss did not have an independent meaningful association with dependency_USP7 or dependency_MDM2 outside TP53-loss context, and PTEN loss did not extend meaningfully to dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, dependency_KIF18A, dependency_DHX9, or TP53-wild-type dependency_MDM2. TP53 loss did not meaningfully predict dependency_MDM2 or dependency_STAT3, and KEAP1 loss did not meaningfully predict dependency_WRN or dependency_STAT3. MSI-high did not meaningfully predict dependency_DHX9, and research markers D, E, and F did not show central meaningful dependency effects, except that research marker F was rejected for dependency_STAT3 and dependency_USP7 and research marker E was rejected for dependency_SMARCA2. Many interaction hypotheses failed to clear the +0.10 benchmark or failed validation, including PTEN-loss by TP53-loss or KEAP1-loss modifications for dependency_STAT3, TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss or mutation-burden modifications for dependency_USP7, SMARCA4-loss interactions for dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss or mutation-burden interactions for dependency_NFE2L2, and MSI-high by SMARCA4-loss for dependency_WRN. These null interactions make the five main associations more credible as central within-dataset patterns rather than diffuse network effects. All conclusions are limited to the supplied dataset. They are associations among measured predictors and CRISPR dependency scores, not causal claims. External generalizability is not established, especially because the dataset is a standardized lung-cancer screen context with constructed assays and markers. Validation improves confidence that the central effects are not simple flukes within the primary split, but it does not establish mechanism or cross-dataset transportability. The most informative next analysis would be external replication in an independent lung-cancer dependency cohort with adequate counts for MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, and PTEN loss. If only the supplied dataset can be used, the highest-value follow-up is a joint adjusted model evaluating all five central predictors simultaneously, with pre-specified interaction terms and multiplicity control, especially PTEN-loss by TP53-loss for dependency_STAT3 and TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss for dependency_USP7. The active registered negative controls H254 through H258 currently have no delivered evidence and do not change this final report; if analyzed, they can provide further outcome-specificity checks for MSI-high and another robustness check for PTEN-loss and dependency_STAT3 in ARID1A-loss cells.

I reassessed H203 using its discovery evidence R208 and validation evidence R216. R208 was directionally supportive but did not clear the pre-specified signed +0.10 meaningfulness benchmark in the supplied dataset, with signed estimate +0.186 and 95% interval +0.039 to +0.333. Independent validation R216 gave a similar point estimate, signed estimate +0.206, but the independent interval crossed both null and the +0.10 benchmark, +0.206 with interval -0.055 to +0.467, and it was based on only 30 exposed cells in the narrow stratum. I therefore keep H203 unresolved and closed. This is a precision problem in a small highly restricted contrast, not evidence against the broader accepted PTEN-loss and dependency_STAT3 association, which was independently validated in much larger comparisons. The overall report is that the supplied 2000-sample lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset supports five large within-dataset associations under the signed +0.10 practical-significance benchmark, while most other predictor-dependency links and interactions are null, small, inconsistent, or too imprecise. First, MSI-high status is strongly associated with more negative dependency_WRN. Discovery R6 gave +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819, and validation R52 gave +0.802 with interval +0.753 to +0.851. The effect is far above the +0.10 threshold and remained supported in multiple refinement contexts, including TP53-wild-type, Avana library, adenocarcinoma, batch A, high-quality RNA/DNA/CRISPR QC, different mutation-burden bands, and several co-mutation-restricted strata. The magnitude and robustness are striking, but this remains an association in this dataset, not proof that MSI status mechanistically causes WRN dependency. Second, SMARCA4 loss is strongly associated with more negative dependency_SMARCA2. Discovery R8 gave +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803, and validation R13 gave +0.793 with interval +0.763 to +0.822. Subgroup refinements across batch A, Avana, KY, adenocarcinoma, QC-restricted, PIK3CA strata, TP53, STK11, CDKN2A, KEAP1, ARID1A, MYC, and multi-negative co-mutation contexts were consistently supportive. By contrast, ARID1A loss did not show a meaningful SMARCA2 association within SMARCA4-wild-type cells, and the ARID1A interaction was null, supporting specificity for SMARCA4 rather than a general chromatin-remodeling loss effect. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2, i.e. less negative dependency scores. H20 accepted this signed positive direction using discovery R20 +0.796 with interval +0.776 to +0.816 and validation R39 +0.806 with interval +0.775 to +0.838. The opposite H9 direction was rejected. This finding is internally consistent across assay, lineage, mutation-burden, co-mutation, and library subsets, although the broader biological interpretation of KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 dependency remains uncertain. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. H15 accepted discovery R17 +0.396 with interval +0.325 to +0.467, and validation R26 was nearly identical, +0.395 with interval +0.293 to +0.498. Multiple refinement strata across library, TP53-cooccurring genotypes, QC, lineage, mutation burden, STK11, CDKN2A, ARID1A, KEAP1, PIK3CA, MYC, MTAP, and co-mutation-negative backgrounds were supportive. The only notable caution is the mutation-burden interaction: the discovery interaction H148 did not provide robust validation, R153 was negative and crossed the benchmark, so I do not support a meaningful TP53-loss by high mutation-burden modification of the USP7 association. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with more negative dependency_STAT3. H93 accepted discovery R88 +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319 and validation R90 +0.329 with interval +0.255 to +0.402. This association was supported in broad, TP53, KRAS, PIK3CA, MYC, KEAP1, ARID1A, MTAP, mutation-burden, QC, batch A, co-mutation-restricted, and multi-negative strata, and validation of some strata such as H102 R179 reinforced the main association. The narrow H203 stratum and the KY-library PTEN-loss stratum H96 remained unresolved because intervals crossed the +0.10 threshold, but these small precision issues do not overturn the broad validated PTEN-loss and STAT3 dependency association. The most important negative and specificity findings are as informative as the accepted associations. Canonical oncogene-concordant dependency was generally not supported: KRAS mutation did not meaningfully predict dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E did not predict dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification did not predict dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification did not predict dependency_ERBB2. Cross-family RTK checks also rejected EGFR amplification as a predictor of dependency_ERBB2 and ERBB2 amplification as a predictor of dependency_EGFR. PIK3CA mutation did not meaningfully predict dependency_ERBB2 after excluding EGFR and ERBB2 amplification. MYC amplification was not clinically meaningful across most tested dependency outcomes, although one tiny opposite-sign WRN contrast appeared; it was far below +0.10 and was not promoted. MTAP loss did not have an independent meaningful association with dependency_USP7 or dependency_MDM2 outside TP53-loss context, and PTEN loss did not extend meaningfully to dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, dependency_KIF18A, dependency_DHX9, or TP53-wild-type dependency_MDM2. TP53 loss did not meaningfully predict dependency_MDM2 or dependency_STAT3, and KEAP1 loss did not meaningfully predict dependency_WRN or dependency_STAT3. MSI-high did not meaningfully predict dependency_DHX9, and research markers D, E, and F did not show central meaningful dependency effects, except that research marker F was rejected for dependency_STAT3 and dependency_USP7 and research marker E was rejected for dependency_SMARCA2. Many interaction hypotheses failed to clear the +0.10 benchmark or failed validation, including PTEN-loss by TP53-loss or KEAP1-loss modifications for dependency_STAT3, TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss or mutation-burden modifications for dependency_USP7, SMARCA4-loss interactions for dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss or mutation-burden interactions for dependency_NFE2L2, and MSI-high by SMARCA4-loss for dependency_WRN. These null interactions make the five main associations more credible as central within-dataset patterns rather than diffuse network effects. All conclusions are limited to the supplied dataset. They are associations among measured predictors and CRISPR dependency scores, not causal claims. External generalizability is not established, especially because the dataset is a standardized lung-cancer screen context with constructed assays and markers. Validation improves confidence that the central effects are not simple flukes within the primary split, but it does not establish mechanism or cross-dataset transportability. The accepted central within-dataset associations remain: MSI-high with stronger dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss with stronger dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7, and PTEN loss with stronger dependency_STAT3. I propose five refinements of these central associations restricted to screens with high quality-control performance, using screen_roc_auc >= 0.95. These test whether the large associations persist when the comparison is confined to screens with better discrimination, thereby reducing measurement-error or poor-screen artifacts. For WRN, SMARCA2, and STAT3, more negative scores mean stronger dependency, so exposed minus comparator is anticipated to be negative for MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, and PTEN loss, respectively; the claims are encoded with direction -1 so a positive signed effect means support for stronger dependency. I also register two outcome-specificity controls: KEAP1 loss on dependency_RPL11 and TP53 loss on dependency_DHX9. These are not mechanistically expected to replicate the accepted marker-specific associations; they test whether the central predictor effects are restricted to accepted outcomes rather than spreading to unrelated ribosomal or replication-helicase dependency phenotypes. Together with the already active final controls H254-H258, these new claims form a concise final robustness and specificity panel. I will judge all new claims using the same practical signed +0.10 dependency-score benchmark: accept only if the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10; reject if the signed upper bound is below +0.10; otherwise leave unresolved. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

I select exactly the 12 active, still-untested claims: H254 through H265. This is the most efficient allocation because these claims complete the specificity and robustness panel around the five central accepted within-dataset associations: MSI-high with stronger dependency_WRN, SMARCA4 loss with stronger dependency_SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss with weaker dependency_NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker dependency_USP7, and PTEN loss with stronger dependency_STAT3. H254-H257 test whether MSI-high shows comparable strong associations with other outcomes KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, and STAT3; acceptance would be a new specificity-relevant observation and would need careful caution, while rejection strengthens outcome specificity of MSI-high for WRN. H258 tests PTEN loss on dependency_STAT3 within ARID1A-loss cells; if accepted, it strengthens robustness of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in a genotype-restricted setting, but if unresolved it would not overturn the broadly accepted H93 evidence. H259-H263 restrict the five central associations to screens with high ROC-AUC quality control (screen_roc_auc >= 0.95); acceptance under the signed +0.10 benchmark would strengthen the view that these are not artifacts of poor-screen measurement, while unresolved precision would leave the broader accepted claims intact. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered comparisons are valid Welch tests with at least 20 observations in every cell and no obvious leakage or coding error: exposures are measured binary predictors, eligibility restrictions use measured screen-quality covariates, and outcomes are the specified dependency scores. I applied the prespecified signed +0.10 practical-significance benchmark: accept only when the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10, reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.10, and leave unresolved when the interval crosses +0.10. H254-H257 reject meaningful MSI-high effects on dependency_KIF18A, dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, and dependency_STAT3; their signed estimates are tiny and intervals are far below +0.10, supporting outcome specificity of the accepted MSI-high/dependency_WRN association. H258 accepts PTEN loss as a meaningful stronger dependency_STAT3 predictor within ARID1A-loss cells, with signed effect +0.268 and lower bound +0.142; this adds genotype-restricted robustness for PTEN loss/STAT3. H259-H263 accept all five central associations restricted to high-quality screens with screen_roc_auc >= 0.95: MSI-high/WRN +0.795, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 +0.790, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 +0.790 in the weaker-dependency direction, TP53-loss/USP7 +0.426 in the weaker-dependency direction, and PTEN-loss/STAT3 +0.239. These are not external independent replications because they are overlapping subsets of the supplied dataset, but they reduce concern that the central associations are artifacts of low-quality CRISPR screens. H264 rejects KEAP1 loss as a meaningful positive predictor of dependency_RPL11, and H265 rejects TP53 loss as a meaningful predictor of dependency_DHX9 despite a statistically small positive signed estimate; its interval remains far below the +0.10 benchmark and therefore does not support a scientifically meaningful association. Overall, these results strengthen specificity and QC robustness of the central within-dataset associations while constraining broader claims. No causal or external generalizability is implied. No validation request was made because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The supplied 2000-sample lung-cancer CRISPR screen supports five large or moderate within-dataset associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The accepted claim set is left unchanged. This report summarizes the strongest evidence-supported conclusions, negative findings, unresolved strata and interactions, and the most informative next analysis. I use the prespecified practical benchmark used throughout the run: an effect is treated as meaningful only when the hypothesis-signed 95% interval lower bound is at least +0.10 dependency-score units; for the central outcomes this is far above the benchmark or, in the USP7 and STAT3 cases, still clearly above +0.10. More negative dependency-score values mean stronger CRISPR dependency. Positive signed effects on NFE2L2 and USP7 mean weaker dependency, whereas positive signed effects on WRN, SMARCA2, and STAT3 mean stronger dependency. All conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability.\n\nSupported findings. Five central associations are accepted and remain the main scientific conclusions.\n1. MSI-high status is strongly associated with stronger dependency_WRN. Discovery R6 gave a signed effect of +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819; independent validation R52 gave +0.802 with interval +0.753 to +0.851. This is the largest and most robust finding. It persisted in many within-dataset refinements, including Avana-library and KY-library contexts, TP53-wild-type and TP53-loss strata, adenocarcinoma, batch A, matched RNA/DNA/CRISPR QC, high-screen-ROC subsets R266, mutation-burden bands, and co-mutation-restricted backgrounds. The magnitude is far above the +0.10 benchmark and above two SDs of the outcome distribution, but this remains a measured association, not evidence that MSI-high causes WRN dependency.\n2. SMARCA4 loss is strongly associated with stronger dependency_SMARCA2. Discovery R8 gave +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803; validation R13 gave +0.793 with interval +0.763 to +0.822. The association was consistently supported across library, lineage, QC, batch, and co-mutation strata. It was also supported in the high-ROC subset R267 with lower bound +0.765. Specificity is important: ARID1A loss did not show a meaningful SMARCA2 association in SMARCA4-wild-type cells, and ARID1A-by-SMARCA4 interactions were null, supporting SMARCA4 rather than generic chromatin-remodeling loss.\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2, meaning less negative scores. The accepted direction is H20: discovery R20 +0.796 with interval +0.776 to +0.816 and validation R39 +0.806 with interval +0.775 to +0.838. The opposite directional claim H9 was rejected. The finding was robust across TP53, STK11, ARID1A, PIK3CA, MYC, MTAP, mutation-burden, lineage, library, QC, and co-mutation-negative strata, and in the high-ROC subset R268 with lower bound +0.763. The biological interpretation of why KEAP1 loss relates to weaker NFE2L2 dependency remains uncertain.\n4. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. A notable caution is the mutation-burden interaction: discovery H148 was only borderline against the benchmark and validation R153 was negative and imprecise, so I do not accept a meaningful TP53-loss-by-mutation-burden modification of the USP7 association.\n5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. Discovery R88 gave +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319; validation R90 gave +0.329 with interval +0.255 to +0.402. In screens with screen_roc_auc >= 0.95, all five accepted associations remained supported: MSI-high/WRN R266 lower +0.758; SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 R267 lower +0.765; KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 R268 lower +0.763; TP53-loss/USP7 R269 lower +0.340; PTEN-loss/STAT3 R270 lower +0.173. These are not external replications because they are subsets of the supplied dataset, but they reduce concern that the associations are artifacts of low-quality CRISPR screens.\n\nNegative and specificity findings. The negative findings are central to interpreting the accepted associations. First, canonical oncogene-concordant dependency was largely absent: KRAS mutation did not meaningfully predict dependency_KRAS overall or in adenocarcinoma or with STK11 loss; BRAF V600E did not predict dependency_BRAF; EGFR amplification did not predict dependency_EGFR, and EGFR-amplification contrasts were too small even when statistically small effects appeared; ERBB2 amplification did not predict dependency_ERBB2. Cross-family receptor-tyrosine-kinase checks also failed, including EGFR amplification versus dependency_ERBB2 and ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_EGFR. PIK3CA mutation was not a meaningful predictor of dependency_ERBB2 after excluding EGFR and ERBB2 amplification. These negatives argue against a broad oncogene-addiction pattern across the tested dependency outcomes.\n\nSecond, MYC amplification was not meaningfully associated with the tested dependency outcomes. It was rejected for KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, TMED10, USP7, and STAT3. A small opposite-sign WRN contrast appeared, but it was far below the practical benchmark and was not promoted.\n\nThird, dependency_MDM2 was not supported by TP53 loss, PTEN loss in TP53-wild-type cells, MYC amplification in TP53-wild-type cells, MTAP loss, or other tested modifiers. This helps isolate TP53 loss to the accepted USP7 association rather than a general TP53-loss dependency network.\n\nFourth, the accepted associations are outcome- and marker-specific. MSI-high did not meaningfully predict dependency_KIF18A, dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, dependency_STAT3, or dependency_DHX9. KEAP1 loss did not meaningfully predict dependency_WRN, dependency_STAT3, dependency_SMARCA2, dependency_USP7 overall, or dependency_RPL11. TP53 loss did not meaningfully predict dependency_MDM2, dependency_STAT3, or dependency_DHX9 at a meaningful size; DHX9 showed only a very small positive signed effect below the benchmark. SMARCA4 loss did not predict dependency_WRN. PTEN loss did not extend meaningfully to dependency_POLR2A, dependency_RPL11, dependency_KIF18A, or dependency_DHX9. USP7 specificity was reinforced by null MTAP-loss, PTEN-loss in TP53-wild-type, and KEAP1-loss contrasts. Research marker D was not a meaningful predictor of dependency_WRN; research marker E was not meaningful for dependency_SMARCA2; research marker F was rejected for dependency_STAT3, dependency_USP7, and dependency_NFE2L2. Validation of research marker F for STAT3 was negative, reinforcing that it should not be interpreted as a biologically meaningful predictor.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. Several claims remain unresolved because of small cell counts or imprecision, not because of contradictory strong evidence. The supplied 2000-sample lung-cancer CRISPR screen supports five large or moderate within-dataset associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. Interaction evidence is mostly null or imprecise. If only this dataset can be used, the highest-value analysis is a joint adjusted model evaluating all five central predictors simultaneously, with pre-specified co-predictor adjustment for co-occurring losses and technical covariates such as library, batch, screen_roc_auc, mutation burden, ploidy or aneuploidy, media-serum, and growth rate, plus multiplicity control and only those interaction terms that receive external validation. No causal mechanism or external generalizability should be claimed from the present evidence."}}

H140 was invalid because of insufficient cells and contributes no evidence.\n\nOverall scientific interpretation. The supplied 2000-sample lung-cancer CRISPR screen supports five large or moderate within-dataset associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. However, the data do not support broad oncogene-addiction patterns, MYC-amplification effects, MDM2 dependency effects, broad MSI-high pleiotropy, or constructed marker effects. The strongest next step would be external replication in an independent lung-cancer dependency cohort with adequate numbers of MSI-high, SMARCA4-loss, KEAP1-loss, TP53-loss, and PTEN-loss samples. No causal mechanism or external generalizability should be claimed from the present evidence."}}

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered comparisons are valid Welch tests with at least 20 observations per cell, measured binary exposures, and measured eligibility/subgroup restrictions; I see no obvious leakage, coding error, or mismatch between the registered hypothesis and the computed contrast. I applied the pre-specified hypothesis-signed +0.10 dependency-score practical benchmark, which also remains conservative if the 10 percent relative clinical-significance notion is considered, because the accepted low-serum effects are far above this scale and the rejected specificity controls remain below it. H266-H270 accept all five low-serum robustness tests: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency (R273 signed effect +0.797, lower +0.750), SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (R274 signed effect +0.761, lower +0.730), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (R275 signed effect +0.771, lower +0.738), TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency (R276 signed effect +0.333, lower +0.218), and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency (R277 signed effect +0.239, lower +0.163). These are overlapping within-dataset subsets, not independent replication, and they do not simultaneously adjust for co-occurring losses, library, batch, growth rate, or aneuploidy, so residual confounding remains possible; however, the signed lower bounds are comfortably above +0.10, reducing concern that the five central associations are confined to high-serum culture contexts. The outcome-specificity controls H271-H277 do not support new practical associations: MSI-high does not show meaningful effects on MDM2 (R278 upper +0.019) or TMED10 (R279 upper +0.016); SMARCA4 loss does not meaningfully predict STAT3 (R280 upper +0.022) or USP7 (R281 upper +0.047); TP53 loss does not meaningfully predict POLR2A (R283 upper +0.006); and PTEN loss does not meaningfully predict WRN (R284 upper +0.038). H275 shows a nominally positive signed KEAP1-loss effect on MDM2 (estimate +0.027, lower +0.004, upper +0.050), but the interval falls entirely below the +0.10 benchmark, so I reject it as scientifically meaningful under the stated decision rule while noting it as a small, possibly nominal, within-dataset signal. Multiplicity has not been formally controlled across the full run, but the consistency of the five central effects, the large lower bounds for accepted robustness checks, and the pre-specified practical threshold argue against treating the rejected specificity controls as meaningful pleiotropy. No validation request is possible or needed because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent-validation budget is exhausted, so this explore step adds a final discovery-only robustness panel. Prior within-dataset robustness checks covered library, screen batch, high screen ROC-AUC, matched omics/QC, lineage, media serum, mutation burden, and many co-mutation-restricted backgrounds. Two scientifically important untested contexts remain: Cas9 activity and chromosomal instability/aneuploidy. If the five accepted central associations are real marker-dependency associations rather than artifacts of imperfect perturbation or particular karyotypic backgrounds, they should remain large in high-Cas9-activity cells and in high-aneuploidy cells. I therefore test each central predictor in eligibility restricted to cas9_activity_score >= 1.0 and in eligibility restricted to aneuploidy_score >= 0.45. The direction convention follows the accepted central claims: MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and PTEN-loss/STAT3 are encoded direction -1 because the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is more negative, while KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 and TP53-loss/USP7 are encoded direction +1 because the expected raw difference is less negative. The two interactions test whether the two most consequential accepted contrasts are modified by screen quality: MSI-high/WRN and PTEN-loss/STAT3 by high screen_roc_auc >= 0.95. Anticipated interaction direction is uncertain; a large interaction would indicate context-dependence, whereas practical rejection would support stability across screen-quality strata. Plausible alternatives are that associations attenuate in high-Cas9 strata if they depend on noisy perturbation, attenuate in high-aneuploidy strata if they are context-dependent, or are technically modified by screen quality. These analyses remain overlapping within-dataset restrictions, not external replication or causal adjustment. For central mean_difference refinements I will use the same practical signed-effect benchmark: accept only if the signed 95% Welch lower bound is at least +0.10 dependency-score units; reject if the signed upper bound is below +0.10; leave unresolved if the interval crosses the benchmark or any cell is insufficient. For interactions I will similarly require a practical signed lower bound at or above +0.10 to accept effect modification; otherwise I will reject as practically unimportant or leave unresolved if imprecise.
